chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And let them fulfill their vows and let them circumambulate the Ancient House,' he said, 'The circumambulation of the women.' And the two rak'ahs of the circumambulation are also obligatory, as evidence for that is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the two rak'ahs of prayer during Hajj circumambulation and do they apply to women?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the Quranic command to circumambulate the 'Ancient House' as explicitly including women, thereby clarifying their specific ritual obligations during Hajj. The hadith further establishes the two rak'ahs of prayer behind Maqam Ibrahim as a mandatory component of the Tawaf, linking the physical act of circumambulation with its associated devotional prayer. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the comprehensive applicability of Quranic verses to all genders while maintaining distinct ritual nuances.
